topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session on the initiation and resolution of inflammation within the Biology of Disease course.

topics.label: Molecular signals of infection and damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define PAMPs and DAMPs and outline the evolutionary criteria used by the innate immune system to distinguish pathogen molecules from self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and intracellular sensing pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the genetics, cellular localization, receptor families, downstream signaling cascades, and inflammasome complexes that detect danger signals.

topics.label: Cellular inflammatory responses and leukocyte trafficking
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct leukocyte recruitment into tissues, drain antigens via lymphatics, and trigger severe systemic complications when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms that shut down acute inflammation, repair damaged tissue, and mediate chronic inflammatory responses such as granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
